theater: 羅馬城東南拉齊亞平原

battle.name: 第一次拉丁戰爭
battle.theater: 羅馬城東南拉齊亞平原
battle.brief: 公元前499至498年，羅馬與拉丁同盟因坎佩尼亞土地爭端開戰，聯軍進逼羅馬城東南的拉齊亞平原。羅馬以三列縱隊配兩翼騎兵與預備隊頂住拉丁騎兵衝鋒，靠預備隊逆轉，攻破大營，逼各城求和。卡面科林斯青銅盔正是這批重裝步兵的頭面裝備：全覆面甲只留窄眼，戰士只能靠百夫長的口令與縱隊的節奏。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 第一次拉丁戰爭（公元前499—498年）是羅馬共和國與拉丁同盟之間的第一場大規模衝突。拉丁同盟是由環繞阿爾巴山朱庇特·拉提亞里斯神域組成的一個城邦聯盟，成員包括圖斯庫盧姆、阿里基亞、蘭烏維烏姆、拉維尼烏姆、佩杜姆、科里奧利、博拉、拉比基、加比、諾門圖姆、科拉西亞等拉丁城市；各城保有自己的軍隊，戰時由同盟會議與同盟執政官統率，政治重心長期在阿爾巴隆加。羅馬一方是推翻王政僅僅第二年的新共和國，軍隊由兩位執政官各領一半，按財產資格徵召的公民兵編為重裝步兵（配大圓盾 scutum、青銅頭盔、長矛與短劍），騎兵則限於富裕階層的騎士團，後勤靠羅馬城外領地（ager Romanus）就地徵發。直接導火線是坎佩尼亞土地爭端：拉丁同盟要求歸還此前被羅馬控制的坎佩尼亞土地，並索回一批扣作人質的貴重物品，羅馬以坎佩尼亞人已自願歸附、處於羅馬庇護之下為由駁回，談判破裂，同盟隨即宣戰。整場衝突都在羅馬城東南數公里內的拉齊亞平原與羅馬城郊展開，雙方營壘相望，一場敗仗就可能直接把敵軍帶到城牆下。
countriesEn: The First Latin War of 499-498 BC was the first large-scale clash between the Roman Republic and the Latin League. The League was a federation of Latin city-states organised around the sanctuary of Jupiter Latiaris on the Alban Mount, and its members included Tusculum, Aricia, Lanuvium, Lavinium, Pedum, Corioli, Bolae, Labici, Gabii, Nomentum and Collatia; every city kept its own levy, and in wartime the host was directed by the league council and by league commanders taken from the aristocracy, with Alba Longa long the political centre of the federation. On the Roman side stood a republic only in its second year after the overthrow of the monarchy. The army was levied by property qualification and split between two consuls, each commanding half of it; the heavy infantry carried the large round shield (scutum), a bronze helmet, the spear and a short sword, while mounted troops were drawn from the wealthier class of equites, and the rear was supplied from the ager Romanus just outside the walls. The immediate occasion of the war was a quarrel over Campanian land: the League demanded the return of territory the Romans had taken once the Campanians had submitted to Roman protection, and demanded the return of valuables held as hostages. The Romans refused, arguing that the Campanians had placed themselves under Roman protection voluntarily, and when the negotiation broke down the League declared war. The whole war was fought in the ager Romanus and in the plain of Latium a few kilometres south-east of the city, with the two camps in sight of each other, so that a single defeat in the field could have brought the enemy to the walls.
people: 羅馬方面的核心人物是執政官盧基烏斯·卡米盧斯（Marcus Camillus 之子），他在這幾年裡連續出任執政官，主持了從議和到營壘佈置的全部軍事決策，也是李維筆下這場戰爭唯一留下姓名的統帥；李維在第二卷為公元前499與498年列出的執政官中，卡米盧斯最為突出（他記載公元前498年由卡米盧斯與塞維利烏斯任執政官，前一年則有西克斯圖斯·維爾吉尼烏斯）。真正決定戰局的是沒有留下姓名的群體：羅馬的騎士團與兩翼預備隊。當拉丁同盟的騎兵擊穿右翼、羅馬騎兵潰散、步兵退向營壘時，正是預備隊的投入把陣線拉回，戰後史家因此把這場仗視為以預備隊取勝最早的典型記錄。拉丁一側沒有常設元帥，命令由同盟執政官下達到各城邦的帶隊者，圖斯庫盧姆與阿里基亞的貴族是主導談判與議和的代表。留下最完整戰場描寫的是公元前一世紀的希臘史家第伊奧尼索斯·哈爾卡納蘇斯，他在《古典集成》第五卷留下這場戰爭的兵力對比、陣形與經過，並且偏袒羅馬，把同盟的慘敗寫成必然，還讓羅馬人自己講出陣形救了我們這類總結。李維《羅馬興亡史》第二卷則把同一場戰爭嵌進王政末期被殺的薩賓婦女、卡比托利歐神廟等前史，讀來更像一則道德寓言。
peopleEn: On the Roman side the central figure is the consul Lucius Camillus, son of Marcus Camillus, who held the consulship repeatedly through these years and took every military decision from the terms of the peace to the layout of the camp; he is the only commander named in Livy's account of this war. In the list of consuls Livy gives for 499 and 498 BC in his second book, Camillus is the most prominent name: Livy records Camillus and Servilius as consuls in 498 BC, and Sextus Virginius in the year before. What really decided the battle were the groups who left no names: the Roman equites and the reserves posted on the wings. When the Latin cavalry broke through the right flank and the Roman horse fled while the infantry withdrew towards the camp, it was the commitment of the reserves that pulled the line back together, and historians have accordingly treated this engagement as the earliest textbook case of victory won by a reserve. The Latins had no permanent field commander; orders came from the league commanders down to the leaders of each contingent, and the nobles of Tusculum and Aricia were the men who handled the negotiations and the peace. The most complete description of the battlefield comes from the Greek historian Dionysius of Halicarnassus in the first century BC, whose Book V of the Roman Antiquities preserves the strength comparison, the formations and the course of the war; he writes as a partisan of Rome, treats the League's crushing defeat as inevitable, and lets the Romans themselves draw the moral that the formation saved them. Livy's second book of the History of Rome embeds the same war in the earlier story of the Sabine women and the Capitoline temple, so that it reads less like a battle narrative than like a moral tale.
kits: 卡面上的科林斯青銅盔是希臘世界重裝步兵的標準防具之一：全覆式面甲，只留兩道窄眼孔與鼻脊的位置，鑄成整體後再裝上頰甲，重量約一點五至兩公斤。這種樣式在公元前八至七世紀出現於科林斯與雅典的工場，經希臘殖民地庫梅（建城約公元前800年）、伊特魯里亞商路與奧西拉陶器貿易逐漸進入意大利中部；到公元前六世紀末，拉丁各城的重裝步兵與羅馬上層公民兵手上出現的已是阿提卡式（眼孔較開、帶護鼻）與科林斯式的希臘樣式，與本土維拉諾沃傳統的鉚接銅盔並存。它在體系中的位置很清楚：不是人人配給的制式裝備，而是公民兵中財產較厚者、也就是羅馬第一序列與拉丁同盟各城富戶的標誌；位階更高的戰士往往另配以名工打造、加飾冠羽的頭盔，羅馬還專門留下頭盔繳獲與分配的做法。武器方面，這場戰爭的近身兵器是青銅與鐵的雙刃短劍（gladius，前五世紀末才逐漸取代伊特魯里亞式的長劍）、長矛、投槍（hasta velitaris）與各城邦的投石索手，盾牌以大圓盾為主，軛甲要到前四世紀才普及。卡面這頂盔正是卡比托利歐地區由盾兵轉向劍士過渡期的典型件：它讓人看不見身側、聽不清口令，所以穿戴者只能靠列陣、靠身旁的百夫長、靠整個縱隊的節奏活下來。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card was one of the standard pieces of armour of the Greek heavy infantry: a fully enclosing face-piece pierced by two narrow eye slits and a ridge for the nose, cast in one piece and fitted with cheek pieces, and weighing roughly one and a half to two kilograms. The type appeared in the workshops of Corinth and Athens in the eighth and seventh centuries BC and reached central Italy by way of the Greek colony of Cumae, founded about 800 BC, the Etruscan trade routes and the exchange of bucchero pottery; by the end of the sixth century BC, the heavy infantry of the Latin cities and the richer Roman citizens were wearing Attic patterns with wider eye openings and a nasal guard, or Corinthian patterns, side by side with the riveted bronze helmets of the indigenous Villanovan tradition. Its place in the system of equipment is quite clear: it was not issue kit for every man but the mark of the better-off citizens, that is, of the Roman first class and of the wealthy households of the Latin cities; men of higher rank often wore helmets made by named craftsmen and fitted with crests, and the Romans kept formal practice in recording and distributing captured helmets. As for weapons, the close-combat arms of this war were the double-edged iron and bronze short sword (gladius, which only gradually replaced the long Italic sword in the late fifth century BC), the spear, the throwing lance (hasta velitaris) and the slingers of the various communities, with the large round shield dominant and mail not becoming common until the fourth century BC. The helmet on the card is a typical piece from the Capitoline region's transition from shield-bearing spearmen to sword-bearing infantry: it leaves a man blind to his own flank and deaf to the word of command, so that the wearer can only stay alive through the line, through the centurion at his side and through the rhythm of the whole cohort.
tactics: 這場戰爭最值得記錄的，是李維與第伊奧尼索斯各自獨立描寫出的一套縱隊加預備隊的戰法。羅馬人把重裝步兵排成三列縱深：第一列是最年輕、裝備最重而經驗最少的青年兵（hastati），向前接敵並消耗敵軍攻勢；第二列是主力（principes）；第三列是老兵（triarii），作為最後一道線；兩翼由騎兵掩護，後方另留兩支預備隊，由騎士與輕裝步兵（velites）組成，一支在右翼、一支在左翼，待正面拉開之後再投入。拉丁同盟照樣排出三列，但把精銳放在兩翼，企圖以人數優勢與騎兵的機動力包抄，計畫的前提是先以右翼突破羅馬左翼，再用騎兵打散羅馬步兵。實際交戰時，羅馬左翼與中央受創，騎兵潰散，陣線一度被拉丁騎兵衝入，步兵退向營壘；關鍵在於拉丁軍追擊時鬆散了原有的縱隊，羅馬預備隊得以從側翼與背面展開，一邊頂住衝鋒，一邊切斷追兵，戰局就此逆轉。營壘在整場戰役中居中樞紐：羅馬營寨依當時習慣築壕溝與土壘（agger），四面設崗哨與巡邏，傷兵與攻城器具留在營內，糧秣靠羅馬領地近運，敵軍遠離本土，無法靠劫掠補足消耗。勝利之後，羅馬沒有遠追，而是以營寨為基地接管戰利品、扣押人質，逼對方派使談判。
tacticsEn: The most remarkable feature of this war is the system of line and reserve that Livy and Dionysius each describe independently. The Romans drew up their heavy infantry in three lines of depth: the first line of young men (hastati), the most heavily equipped and the least experienced, advanced to meet the enemy and to absorb the shock; the second line was the main body (principes); the third was the old soldiers (triarii), the last line of defence; the flanks were covered by cavalry, and behind the lines two reserves were kept, made up of knights and light-armed skirmishers (velites), one on the right and one on the left, to be committed once the front had opened. The Latin League drew up three lines in the same fashion but concentrated its best on the wings, hoping to use its numerical superiority and the mobility of its horse to outflank, on the plan of breaking the Roman left first and then riding down the Roman infantry with the cavalry. In the actual fighting the Roman left and centre were battered, the horse broke up, the line was momentarily pierced by the Latin cavalry and the infantry fell back towards the camp; the turning point was that the Latin army, pursuing, lost its order, and the Roman reserves could deploy from the flank and the rear, holding the charge on one side and cutting off the pursuers on the other, which reversed the battle. The camp was the pivot of the whole operation: the Roman camp was surrounded by a ditch and a rampart (agger) as was the custom, with posts and patrols on every side, the wounded and the siege equipment kept inside, and grain drawn from the nearby ager Romanus, the enemy being too far from its own base to live off the country as it went. After the victory the Romans did not pursue far afield; they used the camp as a base to take over the booty, hold hostages and force the other side to send envoys.
data: 年表方面，李維把這場戰爭放在羅馬建城後第七百五十五與第七百五十四年，即公元前499與498年；第伊奧尼索斯用另一套紀年，把同一場戰爭放在他的前502與501年，兩套紀年相差約三年，這也是本場戰役的定年仍有爭議的原因。時長上，這是一場跨越兩個出征季節的短期戰爭，決戰落在第二年，古代兩部主要史料都沒有記下確切的月日，一般只能按羅馬的出征季節推到春末至初夏。兵員方面，第伊奧尼索斯留下的古代數字把拉丁同盟的步兵寫到數萬之眾，羅馬的步兵寫成八千上下、騎兵八百；這些數字帶著希臘史家的修飾，不宜直接採信，只能當作相對量級的參照，近代研究一般估計公元前六世紀末羅馬一次全軍出征的規模在數千至一萬餘人，騎士數百。騎兵上，李維敘述兩翼攻守時提到羅馬騎兵為數百之眾，這也符合當時羅馬貴族兵力的常見規模。裝備方面，這批重裝步兵的典型配置是長矛一把、大圓盾一面、青銅頭盔一頂、短劍一柄，投槍兵另配輕裝小盾，頭盔重量約一點五至兩公斤。行程與補給上，交戰點距羅馬城東不過數公里，羅馬軍隊每日行軍不超過十數公里，完全依賴羅馬領地與拉丁各城的市集供給，沒有長距離的戰略補給線。
dataEn: As for chronology, Livy places this war in the seven hundred and fifty-fifth and seven hundred and fifty-fourth years from the founding of Rome, that is 499 and 498 BC; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, working from a different era, puts the same war in his 502 and 501 BC, a gap of about three years, which is why the dating of this campaign remains contested. In duration it was a short war spread over two campaigning seasons, with the decisive engagement in the second year; neither of the two principal sources gives an exact month or day, so it can only be placed by the Roman campaigning season, in late spring or early summer. On numbers, the ancient figures left by Dionysius put the Latin infantry in the tens of thousands, the Roman infantry at around eight thousand and the Roman horse at eight hundred; these numbers carry the colouring of a Greek historian and cannot simply be accepted, but they serve as a rough measure of relative scale, while modern estimates generally put a full Roman levy of the late sixth century BC at several thousand to somewhat over ten thousand men with a few hundred horsemen. On the cavalry, Livy speaks of the Roman horse in the fighting on the wings as a force of several hundred, which fits the usual scale of the Roman aristocratic contingent. As for equipment, the typical load of a heavy infantryman was a spear, a large round shield, a bronze helmet and a short sword, with the skirmishers carrying lighter round shields of their own; a helmet of this class weighed around one and a half to two kilograms. As for movement and supply, the ground of the engagement lay only a few kilometres east of Rome, the Roman column never covered more than a dozen kilometres or so in a day, and the army drew everything from the ager Romanus and the markets of the Latin towns: there was no long strategic line of supply at all.
cause: 打起來的直接原因有兩條，一條是土地，一條是榮譽。公元前503年，羅馬與坎佩尼亞的卡普亞訂約，把坎佩尼亞置於羅馬的庇護之下，隨後羅馬公民兵以同盟身分接管了坎佩尼亞的部分土地，並在上面安置移民。這在拉丁同盟看來是越界：拉丁各城長期把坎佩尼亞視為自己的勢力範圍，市場與牧場的歸屬向來敏感。於是同盟派出使節到羅馬，要求歸還所佔土地、並歸還扣作人質的貴重物品，語氣近乎命令。羅馬執政院直接駁回，理由是坎佩尼亞人已自願歸附羅馬，羅馬不承認同盟有權干涉；同時羅馬也反過來翻舊帳，提到同盟方面曾在羅馬城外的卡比托利歐廣場劫走羅馬人的金器，這筆損失從未歸還。當外交手段用盡，同盟便不再等待，以聯軍進軍羅馬領地作開戰，羅馬隨即動員，把兩位執政官各半的縱隊拉到城東，準備在本土迎戰。值得注意的是，這場戰爭並非羅馬主動挑起的遠征，而是同盟把爭端帶到了羅馬的家門口，羅馬因此得以在地利與補給上佔盡便宜——這也是它得以在兵員懸殊之下取勝的結構性原因。
causeEn: There were two immediate causes, one of land and one of honour. In 503 BC Rome concluded a treaty with Capua in Campania that placed Campania under Roman protection, and Roman citizens then took over part of the Campanian territory as allies and settled on it. To the Latin League this looked like encroachment: the Latin cities had long treated Campania as their own sphere of interest, and questions of markets and pasture were always sensitive there. The League accordingly sent envoys to Rome to demand the return of the occupied land and of valuables held as hostages, in a tone that was closer to a command than a request. The Roman senate rejected the demand outright, on the ground that the Campanians had voluntarily submitted to Rome and that the League had no jurisdiction over them; at the same time Rome turned the matter around and recalled that the League had seized the gold of Roman citizens on the Campus Martius outside the city, a loss that had never been made good. Once the diplomatic means were exhausted the League stopped waiting and opened the war by marching its host into the Roman territory, and Rome mobilised at once, drawing up two consular half-columns to the east of the city to meet the enemy on its own ground. It should be noted that this was not a war of Roman aggression; the League carried the dispute to Rome's doorstep, and Rome thus enjoyed every advantage of terrain and supply, which is the structural reason it could win despite being heavily outnumbered.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是拉丁同盟第一次被羅馬正面壓倒，聯盟各城不得不回到談判桌前；它同時把羅馬的戰術傳統固定下來。縱深三列的縱隊、兩翼的騎兵、以及可以及時投入的預備隊，此後成為羅馬對外作戰的基本框架，後世波利比奧斯在二世紀撰寫戰史時仍以此為羅馬戰法的原型，羅馬人自己也把這套以縱深換戰力的做法視為民族傳統中得意的一技。從政治上看，羅馬靠這場勝利在拉齊亞的影響力上升，但正因如此，二十多年後它仍要再打一場拉丁戰爭：公元前524至522年的第二次拉丁戰爭，聯盟在雷吉盧斯湖邊捲土重來，最終敗在同盟執政官奧盧斯·波斯圖米烏斯·圖貝爾圖斯手下。器物層面上，戰勝帶來大量青銅與青銅器戰利品，也讓希臘樣式的頭盔與伊特魯里亞的冶鑄技術在羅馬精英階層中更為普及；科林斯式面甲那種看不見前方的取捨，也在此後數百年裡隨羅馬重裝步兵裝備的演變而逐漸被捨棄——前四世紀以後羅馬的頭盔普遍改為面甲可掀、視野開闊的式樣，羅馬的重心也從持盾的列陣，轉向配備標槍與投石索的散兵。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the war was that the Latin League was beaten in open battle for the first time and its cities had to return to the negotiating table; at the same time the campaign fixed the Roman tactical tradition. The three-deep line, the cavalry on the wings and the reserves that could be committed at the right moment became the framework of Roman warfare at home and abroad; Polybius, writing in the second century BC, still took them as the prototype of Roman tactics, and the Romans themselves regarded this trading of depth for staying power as a point of national pride. Politically the war raised Roman influence in Latium, but precisely for that reason Rome had to fight the Latins again a little more than twenty years later: in the Second Latin War of 524-522 BC the League came back at the shores of Lake Regillus and was defeated by the league commander Aulus Postumius Tubertus. On the level of objects, victory brought in a large haul of bronze and bronze-working, and the Greek pattern helmets and the Etruscan metallurgical skill spread further among the Roman elite; and the bargain of the Corinthian face-piece, that its wearer could not see ahead of himself, was gradually abandoned over the following centuries as Roman heavy infantry equipment changed: from the fourth century BC Roman helmets were generally made with a hinged cheek and a wide field of view, and the Roman centre of gravity moved from the shield-bearing close order to skirmishers equipped with the javelin and the sling.
result: 公元前498年的那場會戰，拉丁聯軍大敗，聯盟大營被攻破，攻城器具與輜重盡為羅馬所得，聯盟的指揮體系一度停擺。此後同盟派出使團到羅馬求和，羅馬提出的條件包括歸還從羅馬人手中掠走的金器、歸還作為人質抵押交出的禮服，並以人質與賠償作為約束；坎佩尼亞的爭端沒有還給聯盟，羅馬保住了對坎佩尼亞的庇護權。戰後沒有合併任何拉丁城市，聯盟的聯邦結構照舊存在，這也是為什麼幾十年後還會有第二次拉丁戰爭。但羅馬從此確立了在拉齊亞平原上的軍事優勢，並在隨後的兩百多年裡逐步走向公元前338年那場最終解散拉丁同盟的戰爭。史料上，這場戰爭的細節幾乎全靠李維與第伊奧尼索斯兩部晚出的作品支撐，考古材料極少：直到今天，羅馬廣場一帶尚未有明確屬於公元前499至498年戰役的戰利品堆積坑，羅馬的地層序列在前六世紀末只能靠青銅器與陶器分期來追蹤。可以確定的是，這兩年裡拉丁同盟第一次承認羅馬可以用兵力和縱隊贏下平原，而羅馬也第一次學會用外交條款把戰場上的勝利固定成不動的邊界。
resultEn: In the engagement of 498 BC the Latin host was routed, the league camp was stormed, and the siege equipment and baggage of the alliance fell into Roman hands; the League's command structure ground to a halt for a time. The League then sent an embassy to Rome to sue for peace, and the Roman terms included the return of the gold carried off from Roman citizens, the return of the cloaks given as pledges of peace, and hostages and compensation as guarantees; the Campanian question was not handed back to the League, and Rome kept its protectorate over Campania. No Latin city was merged or destroyed after the war, and the federal structure of the League survived intact, which is why another Latin war was still possible a few decades later. What did change was that Rome had now established a military superiority on the plain of Latium, and over the following two centuries it moved steadily towards the war of 338 BC that finally dissolved the League. On the evidence, the details of this campaign rest almost entirely on two later works, Livy and Dionysius, and the archaeological material is thin: to this day no clearly identified deposit of booty from a campaign of 499-498 BC has been found in the area of the Roman Forum, and the sequence of levels in Rome for the end of the sixth century BC can only be tracked through the typology of bronze objects and pottery. What can be asserted is that in those two years the Latin League conceded for the first time that Rome could win the plain with numbers and depth of formation, and that Rome learned for the first time to fix a victory won in the field into an unchanging boundary by means of treaty terms.
